site.name: Anna C Mine
site.location: Boulder County Tungsten Mining District, northwest of Nederland
overview: The Anna C Mine was a documented tungsten mine about one and one-half miles northwest of Nederland in Boulder County's tungsten district.

Colorado Geological Survey records describe a 155-foot shaft with three principal levels and production of less than 500 units of tungsten trioxide, while federal exploration records preserve later investigation of the Anna C property.

timeline.text: Anna C was developed on a tungsten-bearing vein in the Boulder County tungsten district, with a main shaft reaching 155 feet and levels at 90, 115, and 155 feet.
A later shallow shaft was sunk at the east edge of the dump and ore was stoped from that working.
Colorado Geological Survey records M. W. MacKenzie as the last operator in 1955.

moreHistory: Colorado Geological Survey MI-04 places Anna C in the southwest quarter of Section 11, Township 1 South, Range 73 West, about one and one-half miles northwest of Nederland. It records O. B. Scott of Rye, Colorado as owner and less than 500 units of WO3 production.

The same state record describes a 155-foot shaft with levels at 90, 115, and 155 feet and notes that most production came from above the 115-foot level. A later shallow shaft at the east edge of the dump also produced ore.

USGS Data Series 1004 preserves federal mineral-exploration files for both the Anna C Mine and Anna C Group in Boulder County, independently confirming the property as a documented tungsten exploration target.
The mapped mine locality near 39.979154, -105.525554 is used as a defensible site-level identification point; Remnant does not claim that this coordinate is a field-surveyed surviving shaft collar.
